newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bank of France trims interest rate; unemployment up.
newsitem.headline: Bank of France trims interest rate; unemployment up.

text.p: The Bank of France said Thursday it was trimming its official intervention rate in what economists read as yet another highly cautious step that left room for further monetary easing as unemployment gained.

The central bank said after a meeting of its monetary policy council that it was cutting the intervention rate by five basis points to 3.20 percent from 3.25 percent, the tenth of a string of small cuts this year.

Fifteen of 20 economists polled by Reuters on Tuesday had said the relatively healthy recent performance of the French franc had provided a "window of opportunity" for a cut and some said news of record unemployment on Thursday morning would only serve to reinforce the issue.

French unemployment hit a record high as 27,700 people applied for jobless benefits in September. The jump announced by the labour ministry was almost double the amount forecast by economists and took the number of workers without jobs up to 3,112,800, pushing the jobless rate to a record 12.6 percent, from a revised 12.5 percent in August.
The gloomy news came just two weeks after a 24-hour strike and demonstrations by tens of thousands of civil servants and other public employees across France over jobs and wages.
"It's really crystal clear, this is really bad," said Valerie Plagnol, an economist at French bank Credit Commercial de France.
The intervention rate, at which the Bank of France allocates repo funds, was last cut, on Sept. 19 from 3.35 percent.
